headline: US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest in two decades
text:
# US electronics factory-gate prices rise fastest in two decades

Chip-adjacent prices in America and household power bills in Austria are the day's outliers; Europe's older energy and car series keep shrinking.

## Today in the data

### Electronics PPI up 12% on the year
[US computer & electronics PPI vs semiconductor output, yoy %](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Computer and electronic products' factory-gate index stood at 118.276 in Jul 2026, up 12.32% on the year (us-ppi-sectors), against a usual +0.57%. On the chart the line has been flat or falling for most of the past fifteen years, so the current spike has no precedent in this series; semiconductor output (us-chips) is up a similar 11.86%. Base periods differ across the PPI series, so read growth rates only.

### Austrian power bills jump a third
[Household electricity price, EUR/kWh, taxes included](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austrian households paid EUR 0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025, up 34.3% on H2 2024 and the largest rise since the record starts in 2008 (energy-household-eu). Luxembourg rose 31.7% to 0.2665 in the same half; Germany, at 0.3869, is still dearer. Taxes and levies are included on purpose, so the jump is worth checking against the expiry of relief measures rather than wholesale prices alone.

### Egypt's FDI gives back last year's surge
[Egypt: net FDI inflows, current US dollars, 1971-2025](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Net FDI into Egypt was USD 15.45bn in 2025, USD 31.1bn below 2024 and the sharpest fall since 1971 (macro-external). The chart shows the fall is mostly the unwinding of a single enormous 2024 spike, not a slide from trend. World Bank current-dollar data lag one to two years and are revised, so treat 2025 as provisional.

### British coal power all but gone
[UK electricity from coal, 1921-2025 (TWh)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
UK coal generation was 0.33 TWh in 2025, down 82.6% on 2024 and the sharpest fall in a record beginning in 1921 (electricity-mix). Gas at 90.91 TWh and wind at 85.84 TWh now sit within a few TWh of each other; coal is a rounding error beside both. The last year is often Ember's provisional figure, and this is generation, not consumption.

### Bulgarian mining output halves
[Bulgaria mining and quarrying output, 2021 = 100](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Bulgaria's mining and quarrying index fell to 50.3 in Jun 2026, 48.3% below Jun 2025 and the sharpest annual fall since 2001 (eu-mining-ipi). The chart shows a series that already swings widely month to month, which makes a single reading a weak signal. Seasonally adjusted Eurostat monthlies are revised, and the July print is due.

### Estonia's car market halves, diesel collapses
[Estonia: new car registrations, total and diesel](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Estonia registered 13,141 new cars in 2025, down 49% on 2024, with diesel at 1,738, down 70.4% (eu-car-registrations). Both are the sharpest falls since the series starts in 2014. Note that 2024 was itself an unusually high year on the chart, so part of the drop is a base effect; a car-tax change is worth checking against.

### Greece past 60% renewable electricity
[Greece: renewable share of electricity, % (2005-2025)](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Greece's renewable share of electricity reached 60.9% in 2025, up 9.65 points on 2024 and the biggest yearly gain since 2005 (eu-renewables-share). The chart's climb is steady from about 10% in 2005, so the size of this step, not its direction, is the news. These are Renewable Energy Directive accounting rules, which differ from generation-based shares.

## Forecasts

### Electronics PPI drifts higher into autumn
[us-ppi-sectors:computer_electronic: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last observation is 118.276 in Jul 2026 (us-ppi-sectors). The tool chose Holt-Winters additive with a 12-month season and fits the past closely, with an in-sample MAPE of 0.215% and residual standard deviation of 0.38 index points. It puts October 2026 at 119.85, in a 95% band of 118.56 to 121.14. The band is only the spread of past one-step errors widened with the horizon, so it says nothing about regime change. A tariff decision, or a reversal in chip prices, would take the outcome outside it.

### Bulgarian mining rebound, on a very wide band
[eu-mining-ipi:BG|B: Holt-Winters forecast, 3 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
The last reading is 50.3 in Jun 2026 (eu-mining-ipi). Holt-Winters additive again wins the auto choice, but fits far more loosely: MAPE 6.8%, residual standard deviation 7.8 index points. September 2026 is projected at 57.4 within a 95% band of 30.8 to 84.0 — a band so wide it covers both a full recovery and a further halving. It reflects only past error spread. The July print, due now, will settle whether June was a one-month stoppage.

### Austrian bills roughly flat next year
[energy-household-eu:AT: Holt-Winters forecast, 2 ahead](https://namikakmandev.github.io/chart.html#)
Austria last printed EUR 0.3272 per kWh in H2 2025 (energy-household-eu). The tool's Holt-Winters fit (MAPE 3.3%) gives 0.3249 for H2 2026, within 0.2904 to 0.3594. This is a taxed, partly administered price, so the projection is an extrapolation of its own past rather than a market forecast. The band assumes the tax and levy structure of recent halves persists; a new relief measure or network-tariff decision would move the price outside it.

## Correlations
- **Austria vs Luxembourg household electricity** (yoy, 2008-S2 to 2025-S2, n=35): r = 0.53 at lag 0 and 0.61 at lag −1, both clearing the 0.359 band. Small euro-area retail markets tend to reprice together, though the peak at lag 4 is likely noise from testing nine lags.
- **US electronics PPI vs semiconductor output** (yoy, 2011-01 to 2026-07, n=187): r = −0.10 at lag 0, strongest |r| only 0.154 at lag 12, not distinguishable from zero. Both are up double digits now, but over fifteen years chip volumes and factory-gate prices do not move together.

## What to watch
- **us-ppi-sectors** (last 2026-07): the August print says whether the 12% electronics jump is a level shift or a spike.
- **eu-mining-ipi** (last 2026-07 for most countries): the July Bulgarian figure settles whether June's 50.3 was a stoppage.
- **us-chips** (last 2026-07): semiconductor IP tells whether volumes keep pace with the price index.
- **cpi-eu and eu-hicp** (last 2026-07): the next release shows whether European energy bills feed into consumer inflation.
- **cattle-eu** (last 2026-08) and **cattle-us / corn-parity** (last 2026-07): due, and untouched by today's outliers.

## Sources
- us-ppi-sectors — BLS producer price indexes by NAICS industry via FRED, not seasonally adjusted, monthly; last 2026-07.
- us-chips — Federal Reserve industrial production via FRED (NAICS 3344, 334), monthly, seasonally adjusted; last 2026-07.
- energy-household-eu — Eurostat nrg_pc_204, band DC, all taxes included, EUR/kWh; last 2025-S2.
- macro-external — World Bank World Development Indicators, FDI net inflows; last 2025.
- electricity-mix — Ember Yearly Electricity Data and Energy Institute Statistical Review via Our World in Data; last 2025.
- eu-mining-ipi — Eurostat sts_inpr_m, 2021 = 100, monthly; last 2026-06 for Bulgaria.
- eu-car-registrations — Eurostat road_eqr_carpda, annual; last 2025.
- eu-renewables-share — Eurostat nrg_ind_ren, annual; last 2025.
